name: Think Like a Coder
promise: Your child will read a program, spot the bug, and think in loops and conditions — the thinking behind every game they play.

sections.title: Sequences
sections.subtitle: A program is a list of steps, and the order is the whole game.

teach.line: Nupo does one step at a time. He starts at the top and works down.
teach.demo: Nupo walks a 3-step program while each block lights up in turn.

questions.prompt: Nupo does these steps. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Put your finger on Nupo. Move it one square for each step.

questions.prompt: Which step does Nupo do first? Tap it.
questions.hint: Nupo always starts at the top of the list.

questions.prompt: How many steps are in this list? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the steps. Do not count the squares.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that takes Nupo to the flag.
questions.hint: Count how many squares up the flag is. Then count across.

questions.prompt: Same steps, but Nupo starts somewhere new. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The steps did not change. Start from his new square.

questions.prompt: Do these two lists end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Try each list from the same square. Only the last one matters.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order so Nupo gets the star.
questions.hint: The star is two squares up and one across. Do both UP steps first.

teach.line: The same steps in a different order can take Nupo somewhere else.
teach.demo: The same three blocks shown twice, in two orders, each running to a different tile.

questions.prompt: Same three steps, new order. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Watch the grey wall. It stops one of them.

questions.prompt: Two steps swapped places. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Read the steps in their new order, from the top.

questions.prompt: Only one of these gets Nupo to the flag. Tap it.
questions.hint: Two of them bump into the wall. Find the one that does not.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to reach the flag.
questions.hint: Which step hits the wall? Think what Nupo should do first.

questions.prompt: No wall this time. Do these two end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Try both. With nothing in the way they may meet up.

questions.prompt: A wall is in the way. Tap the first step Nupo cannot do.
questions.hint: Go one step at a time. Stop when Nupo bumps the wall.

questions.prompt: Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Do every step, right down to the last one.

teach.line: Some steps only work if Nupo did something else first.
teach.demo: Nupo tries to pick up a key he has not reached; the block flashes red.

questions.prompt: This does not work. Tap the first step Nupo cannot do.
questions.hint: Where is Nupo standing when each step happens?

questions.prompt: Which step must happen before OPEN? Tap it.
questions.hint: Nupo needs the key in his hands first.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that picks up the key AND opens the door.
questions.hint: Nupo must stand on the key before he can pick it up.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order so Nupo opens the door.
questions.hint: Walk to the key. Pick it up. Then go to the door.

questions.prompt: Nupo gets to the door with no key. Tap what happens.
questions.hint: A step he cannot do just does not happen.
optionsText: Nothing happens. The door stays shut

questions.prompt: One step is missing. Tap the one that goes in the gap.
questions.hint: What must Nupo be holding when he gets to the door?

questions.prompt: Tap the first step Nupo cannot do.
questions.hint: He walks straight past something he needs.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that gets both stars and then the flag.
questions.hint: Nupo must walk over both stars, not just reach the flag.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to get the star, then the flag.
questions.hint: Pick up the star on the way past.

questions.prompt: Tap the first step that goes wrong.
questions.hint: Look for the step that bumps into the wall.

questions.prompt: Nupo takes four steps right. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Do every step, even the ones after he passes the flag.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest number of steps that reaches the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Find the shortest way there. Then count the steps.

questions.prompt: The dots show where Nupo walked. Put the steps in that order.
questions.hint: Follow the dots from Nupo. Name each move as you go.

teach.line: Nupo does exactly what you say. He never guesses what you meant.
teach.demo: Nupo walks straight into a wall because the program said so.

questions.prompt: A wall is in the way. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: A wall stops that step. Nupo stays put and does the next one.

questions.prompt: Nupo walks into a wall. Tap what he does.
questions.hint: He is not clever enough to go round on his own.
optionsText: He stays put and does the next step
He goes back to the start

questions.prompt: Tap the step that walks into the wall.
questions.hint: Go one step at a time until Nupo bumps.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that gets round the wall to the flag.
questions.hint: Nupo has to go round the wall, not through it.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to get round the wall.
questions.hint: Go up first, then across, then back down.

questions.prompt: Nupo stopped too early. Tap the step that went wrong.
questions.hint: One step tried to walk into the wall.

questions.prompt: No wall this time. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Nothing is in the way, so every step works.

teach.line: Leave one step out and Nupo lands in the wrong place.
teach.demo: A four-step program with one block greyed out; the robot lands one tile short.

questions.prompt: One step is missing. Tap the one that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: Nupo is already across. He just needs to go up.

questions.prompt: This list is one step short. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Just do the steps that are there. Do not add one.

questions.prompt: How many more steps does Nupo need to reach the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the squares between his last square and the flag.

questions.prompt: One step is missing from the middle. Tap the step that fills the gap.
questions.hint: Work out where he must end up, then fill the middle.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that stops on the star.
questions.hint: Check where each one ends. Only one lands on the star.

questions.prompt: He stops one square short of the flag. Tap where he stops.
questions.hint: Do every step in the list and stop there.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order. Cross the star on the way to the flag.
questions.hint: The star is on the way. Go through it, not round it.

teach.line: Steps that undo each other still cost you. Shorter is better.
teach.demo: A program with UP then DOWN highlighted as wasted.

questions.prompt: Tap the step that cancels out the one before it.
questions.hint: One step goes up. The next one takes it straight back.

questions.prompt: How many steps here are wasted? Tap the number.
questions.hint: A step up and a step back down get you nowhere.

questions.prompt: Two of these steps cancel out. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Do them all anyway. He still ends up somewhere.

questions.prompt: Both of these reach the flag. Tap the one that is shorter.
questions.hint: Count the steps in each list. Fewer is better.

questions.prompt: Get the star and then the flag, with no wasted steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The star sits between Nupo and the flag. Go through it.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest steps that reaches the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: The wall is in the way. Count the shortest way round it.

questions.prompt: Reach the flag in exactly 4 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The flag is two squares up and two across. Tap steps to fill the boxes.

questions.prompt: Tap the one step that breaks this list.
questions.hint: Only one step tries to walk into the wall.

questions.prompt: Get the star and then the flag. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The star is on the bottom row. Go along it first.

questions.prompt: Reach the flag in exactly 3 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The flag is three squares across and none up.

questions.prompt: Two steps are missing. Tap the one that fills the FIRST gap.
questions.hint: Work out where he must end up. Then fill the first gap.

questions.prompt: Two walls stand in the way. What is the fewest steps to the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two walls are in the way. Count the shortest way past them.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that is correct AND shortest.
questions.hint: Two of them get there. One does it with no wasted steps.

teach.line: A good coder runs the steps in their head before pressing go.
teach.demo: A program steps forward one line at a time while a finger traces the grid.

questions.prompt: Do not run it. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Move your finger one square per step, from the top of the list.

questions.prompt: A longer list. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Take it slowly. Six steps, one at a time.

questions.prompt: Tap the square this list ends on.
questions.hint: Two across, then two up.

questions.prompt: How many stars does Nupo collect? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He only gets a star if he walks onto its square.

questions.prompt: Same four steps, swapped around. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Trace both from the same square and compare only the end.

questions.prompt: Stop after three steps. Tap the square he is on.
questions.hint: Only do the three steps you can see.

questions.prompt: You expected the flag. Tap the step that ruins it.
questions.hint: One step runs straight into the wall.

teach.line: Look at a path, then work out the steps that made it.
teach.demo: A dotted path draws itself on the grid, then blocks assemble to match it.

questions.prompt: The dots show a three step walk. Put the steps in that order.
questions.hint: Start at Nupo and follow the dots one square at a time.

questions.prompt: A longer path. Put the steps in that order.
questions.hint: Follow the dots to the very end. Watch for the step back down.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that draws this path to the flag.
questions.hint: Trace each one. The wall stops two of them.

questions.prompt: This list matches the path except one gap. Tap the step that fills it.
questions.hint: Look at the square before the gap and the one after it.

questions.prompt: Build a list that gets both stars and then the flag.
questions.hint: Both stars sit on the way. Go across, up, across, up.

questions.prompt: Do the two lists leave Nupo on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Same steps in a different order do not always mean the same path.

questions.prompt: How many steps are in this path? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the steps in the list.

teach.line: Lots of lists work. The best one gets there in the fewest steps.
teach.demo: Two routes to the same flag, one clearly longer, both animating side by side.

questions.prompt: Both reach the flag. Tap the one that is shorter.
questions.hint: Count the steps in each list.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest steps to the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the squares across, then up. Add them together.

questions.prompt: Reach the flag in exactly 5 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: Two across and three up makes five.

questions.prompt: Get the star and then the flag, with none wasted. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The star is on the bottom row, on the way across.

questions.prompt: The wall is in the way. How many steps now? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Going round the wall costs extra steps.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that gets the star AND is shortest.
questions.hint: One misses the star. One gets it the long way round.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest steps past this wall to the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He has to step around the wall and come back down.

questions.prompt: The dots show the path. Put the steps in that order.
questions.hint: Follow the dots from Nupo. Say each move as you go.

questions.prompt: Reach this flag in exactly 5 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: Three across and two up.

questions.prompt: Tap the step that breaks this list.
questions.hint: One step walks straight into the wall.

questions.prompt: Trace it. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Six steps. Take them one at a time.

questions.prompt: What is the fewest steps that gets all three stars and the flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Every star sits on the way. None needs a detour.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that is correct, shortest, and gets the star.
questions.hint: Check the star first, then count the steps.

sections.title: Loops
sections.subtitle: When the same steps repeat, say it once and repeat it.

teach.line: When the same steps come back again and again, use a loop.
teach.demo: A 9-block program collapses into a 3-block loop with a repeat arrow.

questions.prompt: The same two steps keep coming back. Tap where the FIRST pair starts.
questions.hint: Look for the pair that happens again and again.

questions.prompt: How many times does that pair of steps happen? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count how many RIGHT and UP pairs you can see.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that does the same job as the long list.
questions.hint: The long list makes six moves. Count what each loop makes.

questions.prompt: Do the long list and the loop end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Run them both. A loop is just a shorter way to say the same thing.

questions.prompt: Tap the first step that is NOT part of the repeat.
questions.hint: The pattern is RIGHT then UP. Find where that stops.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this loop make in total? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two steps inside, done three times.

questions.prompt: Tap the square this loop ends on.
questions.hint: Do the steps inside. Then go back up and do them again.

teach.line: A loop needs a start and an end. The END row decides what repeats.
teach.demo: Loop brackets slide along the program, highlighting what is inside.

questions.prompt: Tap the last step INSIDE the loop.
questions.hint: The steps inside sit further in than the DO and END lines.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: Two up and two across. Count what each loop actually makes.

questions.prompt: One step sits outside the loop. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Finish the loop first. Then do the step below END.

questions.prompt: How many rows does this listing have? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count every row, including the DO line and the END line.

questions.prompt: How many moves does Nupo make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two steps inside, three times round.

questions.prompt: One step has been moved outside the loop. Do the two still end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: One list repeats both steps. The other repeats only the first.

questions.prompt: A wall stops this loop. Tap the step that hits it.
questions.hint: Go round the loop until Nupo bumps into something.

teach.line: A loop does the same job in far fewer rows.
teach.demo: Side-by-side: 12 blocks versus REPEAT 4 with 3 blocks.

questions.prompt: How many rows does this long list use? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the rows one by one.

questions.prompt: The loop does the same job. How many rows does it use? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the DO row, the step inside, and the END row.

questions.prompt: The loop uses far fewer rows. Do the two end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Run both. If they end in the same place, both are correct.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that reaches the flag with the fewest rows.
questions.hint: They all get there. Count the rows in each.

questions.prompt: This loop goes round twice. Tap the square it ends on.
questions.hint: Two steps inside, twice round.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that reaches this flag.
questions.hint: The flag is three up and three across.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this loop make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: One step inside, four times round.

questions.prompt: Tap the FIRST step of the repeating pattern.
questions.hint: The same two steps run over and over from the very top.

questions.prompt: How many times does that pattern repeat? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the RIGHT and UP pairs.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that does the same as that long list.
questions.hint: The long list makes eight moves.

questions.prompt: This loop goes round four times. Tap the square it ends on.
questions.hint: Across then up, and four goes of it.

questions.prompt: How many moves does that loop make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two inside, four times round.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that gets both stars and the flag.
questions.hint: The stars sit on the way up. Count how far the flag is.

teach.line: DO 4 TIMES means the steps inside run four times. Not three.
teach.demo: A counter ticks 1,2,3,4 as the loop body runs and the robot advances.

questions.prompt: DO 3 TIMES with UP inside. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: One step up, three times over.

questions.prompt: Two steps inside, four goes round. How many moves is that? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two steps inside, four times round.

questions.prompt: Tap the count that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: The flag is four squares up.

questions.prompt: The loop count is missing. Tap the count that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: Count the squares from Nupo up to the flag.

questions.prompt: Three steps inside, twice round. Tap where he ends.
questions.hint: Up, up, across. Then up, up, across again.

questions.prompt: Two loops, different counts, different steps inside. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Count the total moves each one makes.

questions.prompt: How many times do the steps inside run? Tap the number.
questions.hint: The number on the DO row tells you.

teach.line: One time too many, or one too few. The most common bug there is.
teach.demo: The robot overshoots the flag by exactly one tile, then rewinds.

questions.prompt: This loop goes one too far. Tap where Nupo ends.
questions.hint: Do all four, even though the flag is only three up.

questions.prompt: Change the count so he lands on the flag. Tap your answer.
questions.hint: The flag is three squares up.

questions.prompt: Five times round when four was needed. Tap where he stops.
questions.hint: Do all five and see where that leaves him.

questions.prompt: What count reaches this flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the squares from Nupo up to the flag.

questions.prompt: This loop stops one short. Tap the square he stops on.
questions.hint: Only three times round, so only three squares up.

questions.prompt: Nupo lands one square past the flag. What went wrong? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Think about the number on the DO row.
optionsText: The count is one too big
The count is one too small

questions.prompt: One loop goes round once more than the other. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Try both counts and see where each one ends.

teach.line: Work out how far you must go. Then set the count to match.
teach.demo: Distance measured on the grid, then written into the repeat box.

questions.prompt: The flag is 6 squares up. How many times must this loop go round? Tap the number.
questions.hint: One square each time round.

questions.prompt: Now two UP steps sit inside the loop. How many goes round reach the same flag? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two squares each time round, so you need fewer turns.

questions.prompt: Each go round moves one up and one across. Tap the loop that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: Count the squares up, then the squares across.

questions.prompt: Tap the count that gets Nupo both stars and the flag.
questions.hint: The furthest star is also where the flag is.

questions.prompt: Count 3, and UP RIGHT inside. How many moves in total? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two moves each turn, three turns.

questions.prompt: Three goes round, up then across each time. Tap the square it ends on.
questions.hint: Three turns of up-then-across.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that reaches the flag with the fewest turns.
questions.hint: Bigger steps inside mean fewer turns.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop count that gets Nupo to the flag.
questions.hint: Count the squares across to the flag.

questions.prompt: This count is too big. Tap where Nupo actually ends.
questions.hint: Do all five times round, past the flag.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this loop make altogether? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two inside, four turns.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that lands exactly on the flag.
questions.hint: The flag is two up and two across.

questions.prompt: Tap the square this loop finishes on.
questions.hint: Across then up, three turns.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that gets the star and stops on the flag.
questions.hint: The star is on the way up. The flag is further.

teach.line: The inside loop finishes fully every time the outside one goes round.
teach.demo: An outer counter ticks once while the inner counter races 1,2,3.

questions.prompt: A loop inside a loop. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Finish the whole inside loop, then go round the outside one again.

questions.prompt: How many moves does Nupo make in total? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three inside, and the whole lot happens twice.

questions.prompt: Tap the row that starts the INSIDE loop.
questions.hint: The inside loop is the one drawn further in.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that moves Nupo four squares up.
questions.hint: Multiply the outside count by the inside count.

questions.prompt: Tap the square this nested loop ends on.
questions.hint: Two across each time the inside loop runs, and three goes of that.

questions.prompt: A nested loop beside a plain one. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Count the total moves each one makes.

questions.prompt: How many times does the OUTSIDE loop go round? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Read the number on the outer DO row.

teach.line: Outside count times inside count. That is how many times it runs.
teach.demo: A multiplication grid lights up as the loops run.

questions.prompt: How many times does the UP row run altogether? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three lots of four.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this one make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two moves inside, twice, and all of that four times.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that makes exactly six moves.
questions.hint: Multiply the two counts, then multiply by the steps inside.

questions.prompt: Tap the inside count that gets Nupo to the flag.
questions.hint: The flag is six up, and the outside loop runs three times.

questions.prompt: These two nested loops have their counts swapped. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Both make the same number of moves in total.

questions.prompt: Outside 2, inside 3, UP inside. Tap where he ends.
questions.hint: Six ups altogether.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that lands exactly on the flag.
questions.hint: The flag is three up and three across.

teach.line: Nesting helps when a pattern sits inside another pattern.
teach.demo: Nupo draws a square: REPEAT 4 [ forward, turn ].

questions.prompt: Tap the one that reaches the flag four squares up.
questions.hint: Two lots of two makes four.

questions.prompt: Now the flag is four squares across. Tap it.
questions.hint: Same idea, but the step inside has changed.

questions.prompt: How many rows does this nested loop use? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count every row, both DO rows and both END rows.

questions.prompt: Could a plain loop replace this nested one? Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Count the moves each one makes.

questions.prompt: The inside loop goes up twice. Tap the square this one ends on.
questions.hint: Two ups inside, three times over.

questions.prompt: How many moves does that make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two inside, three times over.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that reaches the flag six squares up.
questions.hint: Look for the two counts that multiply to six.

questions.prompt: Trace the nested loop. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Two moves inside, twice, and all of that three times.

questions.prompt: How many moves was that? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Multiply the counts, then multiply by the steps inside.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this nested loop make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three inside, twice over.

questions.prompt: The inside count is missing. Tap the one that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: Six up in total, and the outside loop runs twice.

questions.prompt: Tap the loop that stops exactly on this flag.
questions.hint: The flag is four up and four across.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that collects every star and stops on the flag.
questions.hint: The stars sit on the way up. Count how far the flag is.

sections.title: Conditions
sections.subtitle: Programs make decisions: do this only if that is true.

teach.line: IF checks something first. If it is false, the steps are skipped.
teach.demo: Nupo walks past a star with the IF branch greyed out, then again with it lit.

questions.prompt: Run the steps and tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: The IF only checks. It never moves him.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo pick up the star? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: He is standing on it when the check is made.

questions.prompt: One step in this list never happens. Tap that step.
questions.hint: Nupo is not on a star when the check is made.

questions.prompt: How many stars does Nupo pick up? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Only the ones he is standing on when the check is made.

questions.prompt: The check is made more than once here. How many times does it come back yes? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Look at which squares he lands on, then at which have a star.

questions.prompt: Some rows here are checks, not moves. How many moves does Nupo make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: IF and END are checks, not moves.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo finish on the flag? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Work down the list one row at a time.

teach.line: IF and OR ELSE give two roads. Exactly one is always taken.
teach.demo: The path forks; one branch lights green, the other greys out.

questions.prompt: There is a wall above Nupo. Run the steps and tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: A wall above means the top road is taken, not the bottom one.

questions.prompt: Nothing is above Nupo now. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: No wall above. The check says no, so the OR ELSE road runs.

questions.prompt: Only one of these two roads is walked. Tap the step that does happen.
questions.hint: Look right of Nupo, then read the check.

questions.prompt: The other road is left alone. Tap the step that does not happen.
questions.hint: One road is walked, and the other is passed over.

questions.prompt: Can Nupo step up from where he stands? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Look at the one square directly above him.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo reach the flag? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Walk the road the check picks, then read the rest.

questions.prompt: How many moves does Nupo make in this list? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Each IF lets through one move, and two more follow.

teach.line: A condition can be checked many times and still fire only once.
teach.demo: A loop runs four times; the IF fires on only two of them.

questions.prompt: The check sits inside a loop. How many times is it looked at? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Once on every go round, whatever it says.

questions.prompt: How many of those looks come back yes? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the squares he lands on that have a star.

questions.prompt: How many stars does Nupo end up holding? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He goes past some squares he never lands on.

questions.prompt: The loop goes round whether the check fires or not. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Four goes round, one step across each time.

questions.prompt: This list picks up without checking first. Tap the first step that goes wrong.
questions.hint: Find the first PICK UP made on an empty square.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo pick up every star on the board? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Count the stars, then count the ones he lands on.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that takes the star and stops on the flag.
questions.hint: He must be standing on the star when PICK UP runs.

questions.prompt: How many times does this check come back yes? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He goes round four times and lands on a star twice.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo get through the door? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: He picks the key up on the way.

questions.prompt: Read each check as you go. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: The first check decides which road he starts on.

questions.prompt: One step here is skipped. Tap that step.
questions.hint: Nothing is under him when the check is made.

questions.prompt: Checks are not moves. How many moves does Nupo make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three rows, and all three shift him.

questions.prompt: The PICK UP never happened. Tap the reason why.
questions.hint: Look at the square he was standing on when the check was made.
optionsText: He was not on a star
A wall was in the way

teach.line: A check looks at the square Nupo is on. Or the one beside him.
teach.demo: Nupo stands on a star; the check lights up. He steps off it and the same check goes dark.

questions.prompt: Look at the board. Is Nupo standing on a star right now? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: A check looks at the square under his feet, nothing else.

questions.prompt: The star is further along. Is Nupo standing on it yet? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: The check is made where he is now, not where he is heading.

questions.prompt: Is the square directly above Nupo free? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: A wall there, or the board edge, would stop him.

questions.prompt: Which square does the check ON A STAR look at? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: A check never looks ahead, and never looks back.
optionsText: The square Nupo is standing on

questions.prompt: The check does not move him. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: PICK UP takes the star but leaves him where he is.

questions.prompt: The list checks on every square he lands on. How many times does it say yes? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three landings, and a star waiting on each of them.

questions.prompt: Nupo never picks this star up. Tap the step that is skipped.
questions.hint: There is nothing under him when the check is made.

teach.line: A wall check asks if the next square is free. The board edge counts as a wall.
teach.demo: Nupo meets a wall; the IF road turns him, and the OR ELSE road greys out.

questions.prompt: A wall sits above Nupo. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: A wall above means the check says yes, so the first road runs.

questions.prompt: This board has no wall above him. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Nothing above him. The check says no, so the OR ELSE road runs.

questions.prompt: Two roads, one check. Tap the step that actually runs.
questions.hint: Look above Nupo first, then read the check.

questions.prompt: Is the way up clear for Nupo? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: There is a wall drawn in the square above him.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo land on the flag at the end? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Work down the list, taking whichever road the check picks.

questions.prompt: Does any step in this list fail? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: A step into a wall goes nowhere, and that is a failed step.

questions.prompt: A wall sits in the way on the right. Tap the list that still reaches the flag.
questions.hint: He has to get up and round rather than straight across.

teach.line: NOT reads the check backwards. Blocked becomes clear, clear becomes blocked.
teach.demo: The same board runs twice: once on IF WALL ABOVE, once on IF NOT WALL ABOVE, and he goes opposite ways.

questions.prompt: This check asks if the way up is CLEAR. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Nothing is above him, so the way up is clear.

questions.prompt: The way up is blocked here. Tap the step that happens.
questions.hint: The check wants a clear square above, and does not get one.

questions.prompt: What does the check NO WALL ABOVE ask? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: NOT reads the same check the other way round.

questions.prompt: This list moves right only when Nupo is NOT on a star. How many moves does he make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Four moves up. Add one move right for every go with no star.

questions.prompt: How many times does this NOT check come back yes? Tap the number.
questions.hint: It says yes on every landing square with no star on it.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo stop on the flag? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Read the check each time round, then take the road it picks.

questions.prompt: The way up is blocked, and Nupo must still move. Tap the step that belongs in the OR ELSE row.
questions.hint: The OR ELSE road runs when the way up is not clear.

questions.prompt: Read each check against where he stands. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: The first check decides which road he starts on.

questions.prompt: Does the door open for Nupo? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: He needs to be carrying the key by the time he reaches it.

questions.prompt: Nupo gets stuck on this board. Tap the first step that fails.
questions.hint: Follow him along the row until a wall is in his way.

questions.prompt: How many stars does Nupo end up with? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Five goes round, and a star on only some of the squares.

questions.prompt: This list should pick a star up whenever Nupo lands on one. Tap the check that belongs in the IF row.
questions.hint: The check has to ask about the square he is standing on.

questions.prompt: One step here is never reached. Tap it.
questions.hint: The check is made on a square with nothing on it.

teach.line: A check inside a check. The step only happens when both say yes.
teach.demo: Nupo walks a row of stars and picks up only the ones with a wall above them.

questions.prompt: Nupo picks a star up only if a wall sits above it too. How many stars does he pick up? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two stars on the row. Look above each one before you count it.

questions.prompt: Is every star on this board collected? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: One of the two stars has open sky above it.

questions.prompt: On this board BOTH stars have a wall above them. How many does Nupo pick up now? Tap the number.
questions.hint: When both checks say yes, the step goes ahead.

questions.prompt: Nupo is on a star, but nothing is above him. Tap the step that never happens.
questions.hint: The outer check says yes. The inner one does not.

questions.prompt: The inner check came back no. What happens to the PICK UP? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Both checks have to say yes before the step inside them runs.

questions.prompt: Count every check made here, the inner ones too. How many are there? Tap the number.
questions.hint: The inner check is only looked at when the outer one says yes.

questions.prompt: The star must have a wall above it too. Tap the check for the inner IF row.
questions.hint: The outer check already asks about the star.

teach.line: Two roads to the same step. Either check can send him down its road.
teach.demo: The same step sits at the end of the IF road and the OR ELSE road; whichever check fires, he takes it.

questions.prompt: Nupo moves up when the way right is blocked. Or when a star is under him. Here the board edge counts as a wall. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The first check is enough on its own.

questions.prompt: The way right is clear here, but Nupo is on a star. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The second road leads to the same step as the first.

questions.prompt: The way right is clear and there is no star. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: Neither check says yes, so neither road is walked.

questions.prompt: Neither check fired. Does Nupo still reach the flag? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Check both roads before you decide he stays put.

questions.prompt: Two roads end at the same step. How many checks must say yes for it to run? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Either road on its own gets him there.

questions.prompt: How many moves does this loop make in all? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three goes round, and a star under him on some of them.

questions.prompt: Nupo must move up on either road. Tap the step that belongs on the second road.
questions.hint: Both roads must end at the same step. Otherwise only one check counts.

teach.line: Real ones use both. Two checks can guard one step, or reach it.
teach.demo: One board, run twice: once with the checks nested, once with them side by side, ending differently.

questions.prompt: Again a star is picked up only when a wall sits above it. How many stars does Nupo pick up? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three stars along the row, and a wall above only some of them.

questions.prompt: This list moves up if the way right is blocked. Or if Nupo is on a star. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The star lets the move through, and two more steps follow.

questions.prompt: Two lists, one board. Do they finish on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Run each one from the top and compare only where he stops.

questions.prompt: Is Nupo standing on a star right now? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: With OR, this check on its own would be enough.

questions.prompt: Only one star here, and a wall above it. How many stars does Nupo pick up? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Both checks say yes on the square where the star sits.

questions.prompt: How many times is a check looked at on this board? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three goes round, and the inner check is not always reached.

questions.prompt: Nupo must pick this star up whether or not anything sits above it. Tap the check that belongs in the IF row.
questions.hint: One check is enough when the other is not wanted.

questions.prompt: Same rule again: a wall must sit above the star. How many stars does Nupo pick up? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Move one square at a time and check both things each go.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo end up holding all three stars? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: Only the stars with something directly above them count.

questions.prompt: Either check sends Nupo up: way right blocked, or a star underfoot. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The board edge counts as blocked.

questions.prompt: Nupo reaches the star, but the sky above it is open. Tap the step that never happens.
questions.hint: The inner check is the one that turns it down.

questions.prompt: How many moves does Nupo make on this board? Tap the number.
questions.hint: The checks are not moves. Count only the rows that shift him.

questions.prompt: Does Nupo stop on the flag square? Tap Yes or No.
questions.hint: The star opens the second road, then one more step follows.

sections.title: Debugging
sections.subtitle: Programs go wrong. Finding out why is the real skill.

teach.line: To find a bug, run it and watch where it stops making sense.
teach.demo: The robot runs, hits a wall, and the offending block flashes red.

questions.prompt: Before you run it: tap the square you think he ends on.
questions.hint: Follow the steps in your head, wall and all.

questions.prompt: Run it. Tap the step where it goes wrong.
questions.hint: Walk it until Nupo bumps into something.

questions.prompt: This one has no wall. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Nothing is in the way, so every step works.

questions.prompt: He stops short of the flag. Tap the step that fails.
questions.hint: One step tries to walk through the wall.

questions.prompt: One wall, one flag. Tap the list that gets there.
questions.hint: He has to go under or over the wall, not through it.

questions.prompt: How many moves happen before the wall stops him? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the steps that actually move him.

questions.prompt: Tap the square he is stuck on.
questions.hint: The blocked step does nothing, and the ones after it repeat the problem.

teach.line: Once one step is wrong, every step after it looks wrong too.
teach.demo: Two paths diverge at one point, the split highlighted.

questions.prompt: This list stops one square short of the flag. Tap what is wrong with it.
questions.hint: Count the squares to the flag, then count the steps.
optionsText: There is a step too many
The steps are in the wrong order

questions.prompt: Tap the step that fills the gap and lands him on the flag.
questions.hint: Look at the square before the gap and the flag after it.

questions.prompt: This list goes one square past the flag. Tap what is wrong with it.
questions.hint: It does everything the flag needs, and then one thing more.
optionsText: There is a step too many
The steps are in the wrong order

questions.prompt: This list walks into a wall. Tap the first step that fails.
questions.hint: Go from the top and stop at the first bump.

questions.prompt: The same four steps, in three orders. Tap the one that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: The wall sits directly above the middle square.

questions.prompt: This loop counts wrong. Tap the count that lands him on the flag.
questions.hint: Count the squares between Nupo and the flag.

questions.prompt: How many moves does the broken list actually make? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Blocked steps still count as steps, but they move him nowhere.

teach.line: Say what you think will happen. If you are wrong, you found a bug.
teach.demo: A prediction is placed on a tile, then the run shows a different tile.

questions.prompt: Where do you think it ends? Tap that square.
questions.hint: Trace it before you look at anything else.

questions.prompt: Now this one, with a wall. Tap where he really ends.
questions.hint: The wall changes the answer. Take it one step at a time.

questions.prompt: Your guess and the run differ. Tap the step where.
questions.hint: Find the first step that could not do what you expected.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that gets to the flag with that wall there.
questions.hint: He has to go up before he goes across.

questions.prompt: After the fix, tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: This one has nothing in the way.

questions.prompt: A long list beside a loop. Do they end on the same square? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: Run both and compare only the last square.

questions.prompt: Your guess and the run disagree. Tap what that means.
questions.hint: That is the whole point of guessing first.
optionsText: A bug, or something you misread

questions.prompt: Tap the first wrong step.
questions.hint: Two things are in the way. Only one stops him first.

questions.prompt: Tap the square that broken list leaves him on.
questions.hint: Keep going after the bump. The later steps still try.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to get the star and the flag.
questions.hint: The star sits on the diagonal, so go up and across in turns.

questions.prompt: This loop hits a wall. Tap the step inside it that fails.
questions.hint: The step inside runs four times, but one of those runs bumps.

questions.prompt: How many moves does the loop make in total? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Blocked runs still count as moves.

questions.prompt: Tap the list that gets round this wall to the flag.
questions.hint: Go along the bottom first, then up at the end.

teach.line: A box holds a number. You can look inside, and you can change it.
teach.demo: A box labelled COINS shows 0, then 1, then 2 as stars are collected.

questions.prompt: Nupo adds one to the box for every star he picks up. What is in STARS at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the ADD rows, or count the stars. They agree.

questions.prompt: This box does not start empty. What is in it at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Start from the number already in the box, then add.

questions.prompt: Tap the FIRST row that changes what is in the box.
questions.hint: Only an ADD row touches the box. Moving and picking up do not.

questions.prompt: Nupo moves right. What does that row do to STARS? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: A row has to name the box before it can change it.

questions.prompt: He walks over one star without picking it up. What is in STARS at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: The box only counts what an ADD row counts.

questions.prompt: Two boxes on this board. What is in KEYS at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Read only the rows that say KEYS.

questions.prompt: Follow STARS down the list. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: Look at the row above the blank, and the one step between them.

teach.line: SET puts a new number in. ADD changes the one already there.
teach.demo: SET replaces the number; ADD stacks onto it, shown side by side.

questions.prompt: The box already holds 5. This row SETS it to 2. What is in it now? Tap the number.
questions.hint: SET throws away what was there.

questions.prompt: The box holds 5 again, but now the row ADDS 2. What is in it now? Tap the number.
questions.hint: ADD keeps what was there and builds on it.

questions.prompt: Tap the row that throws away what the box already held.
questions.hint: One of these three rows does not care what was in the box.

questions.prompt: SET first, then two ADD rows. What is in the box at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Start from the SET, not from zero.

questions.prompt: Two SET rows in a row. What became of the first number? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: SET does not care what was in the box before it.
optionsText: It was added to the second one
It is still in the box

questions.prompt: ADD can take away too. What is left in the box? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Take three off first, then two more.

questions.prompt: The SET row sits in the middle. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: Read the row above the blank, then do the one step between them.

teach.line: Write down what the box holds at each step. The bug shows up.
teach.demo: A trace table fills in row by row as the program steps.

questions.prompt: One row of this table is blank. Tap the number that belongs there.
questions.hint: Each row adds to the row above it.

questions.prompt: A loop with an ADD inside. What ends up in COINS? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three times round, three lots added, on top of what it started with.

questions.prompt: The moves leave the box alone. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: Only the ADD rows change it. The rest hold it steady.

questions.prompt: Two boxes now. What is in COINS at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Read only the rows that say COINS.

questions.prompt: And what is in KEYS? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Only one row in this list touches KEYS.

questions.prompt: This list has move rows and ADD rows. Which kind changes STARS? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: A row has to name the box before it can change it.

questions.prompt: This list takes away instead of adding. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: Each row takes three off the row above it.

questions.prompt: A SET row, then two ADD rows. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: The SET row does not care what was above it.

questions.prompt: What is the final value in COINS? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Work down from the SET row to the bottom.

questions.prompt: A loop adding 5, four times round. What is in the box at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Four lots of five.

questions.prompt: It should end at 12 but ends at 7. Tap the row that spoils it.
questions.hint: One row throws away everything above it.

questions.prompt: How many times does the value change inside this loop? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Once on every go round.

questions.prompt: The box counts the stars again. What is in STARS at the end? Tap the number.
questions.hint: One ADD row under every PICK UP.

teach.line: Big jobs are small jobs stacked up. Do them one at a time.
teach.demo: A long level splits visually into three lit segments, solved one by one.

questions.prompt: This level needs a key, a door and a flag. What comes first? Tap your answer.
questions.hint: You cannot open the door without the thing that opens it.

questions.prompt: Nupo must fetch the key, open the door, then reach the flag. How many jobs is that? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the things named in the question.

questions.prompt: Here is just the first job. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Only these three rows run.

questions.prompt: Build just the first part: get to the key and pick it up.
questions.hint: Two steps across, then pick it up.

questions.prompt: Tap the order that does all three jobs.
questions.hint: Key first, then the door, then the flag.

questions.prompt: How many steps does the whole level take? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count the shortest way from Nupo to the flag.

questions.prompt: This list does the first two jobs only. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: He fetches the key and opens the door, and stops there.

teach.line: Steps you keep using deserve a name you can use again.
teach.demo: Three identical block groups collapse into one named CLIMB block, used three times.

questions.prompt: The same two steps appear three times, but never side by side. Tap where the FIRST pair starts.
questions.hint: Look for the pair that keeps coming back further down.

questions.prompt: How many rows does this list use in full? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Count them one by one.

questions.prompt: A loop cannot shorten this list. Tap the reason why.
questions.hint: Look at what sits between one pair and the next.
optionsText: The pairs are not next to each other

questions.prompt: The chunk is 2 steps and Nupo uses it 3 times. How many steps is that in all? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two steps, three goes.

questions.prompt: Run the whole list. Tap the square Nupo ends on.
questions.hint: The steps in between move him too.

questions.prompt: Here the chunk repeats side by side. A loop does fit this time. Tap the loop that reaches the flag.
questions.hint: The flag is three up and three across.

questions.prompt: Use the chunk twice to reach the flag in exactly 4 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: The chunk is one up and one across. Do it twice.

teach.line: Real ones use steps, loops, conditions and boxes together.
teach.demo: A full level runs end to end using every idea from the skill.

questions.prompt: A loop with a condition inside. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: The moves happen every time round. The pick only sometimes.

questions.prompt: How many stars does that collect? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He checks on every square he steps onto.

questions.prompt: A loop with a box inside. What ends up in COINS? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two added each time, three times round.

questions.prompt: Tap the one that gets round the wall to the flag.
questions.hint: The wall sits on the diagonal, so go along one side.

questions.prompt: Loop, move and box together. Tap where he ends.
questions.hint: Only the move rows change where he is.

questions.prompt: Tap the number that belongs in the blank row of this table.
questions.hint: Only the ADD rows change the number.

questions.prompt: How many moves does that loop make in total? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Two rows inside, twice round.

questions.prompt: Everything at once. Tap the square he ends on.
questions.hint: Up and across each time round, three times over.

questions.prompt: How many stars does that list collect? Tap the number.
questions.hint: He only picks up when he is standing on one.

questions.prompt: Four goes round, adding each time. What is left in COINS? Tap the number.
questions.hint: Three added, four times round.

questions.prompt: Use the named chunk twice to reach the flag in exactly 4 steps. Drag the steps into order.
questions.hint: Two up and two across.

questions.prompt: One list fetches the key, opens the door and reaches the flag. Tap it.
questions.hint: Key first. Then the door. Then the flag.

questions.prompt: Last one. Tap the number for the blank row.
questions.hint: Three added every time round.
